correctness.rationale: Direct distance/geodesic argument: for |S|>=3 a supporting cycle site cannot have both root and leaf. A leaf is never geodesic interior; root at occupied site j can occur exactly if 2(g_(j-1)+g_j)>n, including the tied-path equality as forbidden. Thus each k-subset of supporting sites contributes 2^{eligible roots}. Marking eligible single roots, adjacent pairs and (only k=3) triples yields the stated U,V,W correction formula; nonadjacent eligible roots for k>=4 are impossible by disjoint gap sums >n. Low-degree coefficients and the n=3 vs n>=4 top coefficients checked. Independently computed all vertex-subset distances for n=3..6; obtained the source coefficient vectors exactly, and inspected the original verification program covering n=3..9. This proof, not finite checks, supports all n>=3.

originality.rationale: The original general-position polynomial theory and comb/path-corona formulas do not furnish the cyclic-gap classification for all cycle coronas. Rather already publishes exactly the n=6 polynomial, which is excluded from the novel part. A generic inclusion-exclusion enumerator is not the specialized all-n, polynomial-time coefficient formula; Resultary nearest related records treat complete-graph coronas and spiders. Best-of-knowledge original contribution: all-cardinality cyclic-gap bijection and explicit finite sums for every n.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalent all-n sunlet coefficient formula possible.
Finite verifier ends at bounded graph sizes; generality is proved analytically.

value.rationale: Cycle coronas are the natural cyclic counterpart of path coronas in the initiating literature; computing their complete general-position polynomial, not merely its maximum-set size, is a motivated exact natural graph invariant. The cyclic-gap criterion and O(n^4) coefficient arithmetic provide structural and computational value for the unresolved general corona-unimodality question, without claiming unimodality.
